---
title: "Header"
---

The optional `header` block holds the lines above the table: a title, a subtitle, and
any number of extra lines, in that order.

## Structure

```json
{
  "header": {
    "title": { "content": [{ "type": "text", "value": "Regional Sales" }] },
    "subtitle": { "content": [{ "type": "text", "value": "Fiscal year 2024" }] },
    "extra_lines": [
      { "content": [{ "type": "text", "value": "Preliminary figures" }], "style_id": "note" }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Fields

<!-- ir-fields: Header -->

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `title` | HeaderLine? | `null` | The title |
| `subtitle` | HeaderLine? | `null` | The subtitle, below the title |
| `extra_lines` | array of HeaderLine | `[]` | More lines below the subtitle, in order |
| `preheader_content` | any? | `null` | Anything a producer wants to carry along with the header. No writer reads it, and it round-trips unchanged |

### Header lines

<!-- ir-fields: HeaderLine -->

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `content` | array of [content nodes](index.qmd#content-nodes) | required | The line's content |
| `style_id` | string? | `null` | The line's style |

A line's content may hold footnote marks; they must refer to a defined footnote
(`FOOTNOTE_REFS_VALID`). In HTML the title names the table for screen readers
(`aria-labelledby`) and the subtitle describes it (`aria-describedby`), unless
`config.aria_label`, `config.summary` or `config.aria_describedby` says otherwise.
